events.description: An authorized S3 team member executed a command using an established playbook to remove a small number of servers for an S3 subsystem used by the billing process; an input was entered incorrectly and a larger set of servers was removed than intended.
The removed servers supported the index subsystem and the placement subsystem, causing removal of a significant portion of capacity, which required both subsystems to undergo a full restart.
S3 was unable to service requests, and other AWS services in US-EAST-1 relying on S3 (S3 console, EC2 new instance launches, EBS volumes needing S3 snapshot data, and AWS Lambda) were impacted.

events.time: From the beginning of the event until 11:37AM PST
events.description: The team was unable to update individual service status on the AWS Service Health Dashboard due to a dependency on Amazon S3; status was communicated via the @AWSCloud Twitter feed and SHD banner text.
The team regained the ability to update individual services' status on the AWS Service Health Dashboard.
The index subsystem activated enough capacity to begin servicing S3 GET, LIST, and DELETE requests.
The index subsystem was fully recovered and GET, LIST, and DELETE APIs were functioning normally.
The placement subsystem began recovery, as the S3 PUT API required it.
The placement subsystem finished recovery and S3 was operating normally.
Other impacted AWS services began recovering, with some requiring additional time to clear an accumulated backlog of work.
